reason: the shared cage matches UPDATE so that a forged `posture.acme.io/tier` label on a running pod is clobbered back to its Namespace's rung -- the pod label is an OUTPUT only. For a pod whose rung has not changed the mutation writes exactly what the pod already carries, which is why it is admitted and why leg B measures byte-identity on every run. It differs only when the pod's rung CHANGES under it, and the one way that happens is ticket 89's live instance: a pod the guard caged on the bottom rung is given a served-version claim, so `cage-tier` takes it over and rewrites `tier: isolated -> baseline`, `priorityClassName: cage-isolated -> cage-baseline-4-0-0` and `priority: -10000 -> -10`. The last two are immutable on a running pod and the API server refuses the edit. Ticket 89 (S3, delegated, 2026-09-05) decided the refusal is CORRECT: letting it through would be a workload moving itself off the bottom rung by asserting a label, which is the self-service exemption principle 1 bans. A pod's cage is written at admission from what it declared then
remediation: recreate the pod with the claim declared, which is the route CONTEXT.md's De-postured entry already describes -- adding a label to a running pod is not a remediation and never was

bounded by: leg B (refusal_probe.py) applies each of these bodies to its own output on every run and requires the result to be identical. The acceptance covers a value that CHANGES; it does not cover a body that rewrites a pod it has already caged, and the day one does, leg B goes red rather than this row growing to cover it
